# Switch

An on or off setting that applies at once, with no submit.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Dense data</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-switch--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:light" title="Switch examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-switch--docs">Open Switch in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-switch--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Dense data:** Settings that apply at once.

- **Use it when:** A setting that should take effect as soon as it is flipped.
- **Not when:** A choice that waits for a form (checkbox).

Instead:

- [Checkbox](./checkbox.md): Waits for the form.
- [Toggle](./toggle.md): A pressed button in a toolbar.

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| undefined | Space flips it. | undefined |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It is a switch with a visible label; on and off are announced. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add switch
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Variables

Every token Switch reads, from its code: the variable, the semantic token it aliases, and where that ends in the theme.
